coordinates.note: No primary or official source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) gives numeric coordinates for the underground lab itself: the abstract of the SAGE 1999 results paper does not state them, and the official Baksan/INR site returned 404. The point is the Wikipedia infobox coordinate for the laboratory area, so it is a campus-grade, approximate point and not an underground-laboratory position. A published survey or an official INR coordinate would give a better one.

depth.display: ~2100 m of rock above the laboratory
depth.locator: Slide 'Baksan Valley and Mt. Andyrchi' (page 7 of the PDF)
depth.note: Rock thickness above the SAGE (GGNT) laboratory per the Baksan Neutrino Observatory's 2016 presentation; the SAGE 1999 paper gives the overburden as 4700 m.w.e. (see depth_mwe). Earlier source: Wikipedia (rank 12), now dropped from this field.
depth.quote: GGNT - 3,5 km from the entrance 2100 m thickness of the rock above laboratory (4700 m.w.e.)

depth_mwe.note: Overhead shielding of the SAGE gallium laboratory, 3.5 km from the entrance of the horizontal adit into Mount Andyrchi (SAGE 1999 results paper).
depth_mwe.quote: has an overhead shielding of 4700 meters of water equivalent

summary.plain: A chamber more than two kilometres inside a mountain in the Russian Caucasus, holding tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch solar neutrinos.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory of the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, ~2100 m (6900 ft) underground in the Caucasus Mountains, Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia, housing the SAGE gallium detector.
